literal: If one is indeed a lover of oneself, let one not approach the side of evil deeds, even in the slightest measure.
translation: If a person truly loves themselves, let them not approach the path of evil deeds, even in the slightest degree.
modern: ஒருவன் தன்னைத்தானே நேசிப்பவனாக இருந்தால், எவ்வளவும் சிறியதான தீய செயல்களின் பக்கமும் அவன் நெருங்காமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet explains that true self-love lies in protecting oneself from harm, which can only be achieved by avoiding bad deeds. The word 'kātalaṉ' refers to one who loves, here meaning someone who desires their own true well-being. If a person has this genuine love for themselves, they must not commit any 'tīviṉai' (evil deed), even a tiny fraction ('eṉaittu oṉṟum'). Avoiding the path of evil is presented as the ultimate act of self-preservation, as evil deeds inevitably bring ruin to the doer.
